original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Remove the duplicate pinned-catalogue Git read from complete research-draft creation, preserving generated bytes and source/output rejection contracts.
scope_change_reason: The replay-runtime card is narrowed to one original generator optimization after live overlap excluded recent-account mathematical follow-ups.
bottleneck_link: Reduce onboarding overhead without reducing source binding or replay coverage; this is tooling and changes no multiplication bound.
stop_rule: Ship the first complete-command gain beyond observed noise with exact five-file comparisons and rejecting controls; do not extend the optimization.
evidence: MEASUREMENTS.json: 31 alternating pairs per workload, zero errors/mismatches, 14.55% and 13.49% median wall-time reductions. Direct verifier checks 3 differential cases and 9 guard tests.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Does a workload with hundreds of explicit sources remain dominated by the batched reader rather than the removed catalogue read?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The measured result covers default and eight-source drafts; the relative gain may shrink for source-heavy packages.
open_questions.first_step: Select one actual large package source inventory, materialize its exact paths, and measure the same complete CLI with output equality.
open_questions.blocked_by: A separately budgeted representative workload and current overlap check.

claim_type: empirical tooling improvement with a scoped source-level equivalence argument

overlap.limitation: Sparse local overlap cache is incomplete; whole-main README searches and targeted live all-state PR searches supplement it.
